summary: May we leave a pot on a stove on Shabbos? It depends on what the fire was made with and whether the coals were swept away. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about what may be left there and whether a pot may be put back.

chunks.en: A stove that was heated with straw or stubble,
chunks.st: a stove that was lit on Shabbat eve with straw or with rakings, scraps collected from the field,

words.note: Little scraps of plants left in the field.

chunks.en: we may put cooked food on it.
chunks.st: one may place a pot of cooked food atop it
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat. The fire in this stove was certainly extinguished while it was still day, as both straw and rakings are materials that burn quickly.

chunks.en: If it was heated with olive pulp or with wood,
chunks.st: However, if the stove was lit with pomace, pulp that remains from sesame seeds, olives, and the like after the oil is squeezed from them, and if it was lit with wood,

chunks.en: one may not put food on it until he sweeps out the coals,
chunks.st: one may not place a pot atop it on Shabbat until he sweeps
chunks.stMore: the coals from the stove while it is still day

chunks.en: or until he puts ashes on them.
chunks.st: or until he places ashes
chunks.stMore: on the coals, so that the fire will not ignite on Shabbat.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:
chunks.stMore: Even after one has swept away the coals, it is only permitted to place

chunks.en: hot water, but not cooked food.
chunks.st: hot water on it, as it is sufficiently hot and does not require additional cooking, but not cooked food.
chunks.stMore: Since, in general, one prefers that food will cook more, there is concern lest he come to ignite the fire by stoking the coals.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say: Both

chunks.en: hot water and cooked food.
chunks.st: hot water and cooked food may be placed.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we may take a pot off, but we may not put it back.
chunks.st: One may remove a pot from the stove on Shabbat but may not return it.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say: One may

chunks.en: we may even put it back.
chunks.st: even return it.

summary: An oven holds a lot of heat, so even if it was heated with straw, nothing may be put in it or on it on Shabbos. A smaller stove called a kupach depends on what it was heated with.
stIntro: The halakhot that were stated with regard to a stove were specific to a stove’s unique structure and the manner in which it retains heat. However, with regard to other baking apparatuses, i.e., an oven or a kupaḥ, there are different rules. The mishna delineates:

chunks.en: An oven that was heated with straw or stubble,
chunks.st: An oven that they lit even with straw or rakings,

chunks.en: one may not put food either inside it
chunks.st: one may neither place a pot inside it

chunks.en: or on top of it.
chunks.st: nor atop it on Shabbat. Whereas a

chunks.en: A kupach that was heated with straw or stubble
chunks.st: kupaḥ that was lit with straw or rakings,

words.note: A small stove for one pot.

chunks.en: is like a stove.
chunks.st: its legal status is like that of a stove,
chunks.stMore: and one is permitted to place a pot atop it on Shabbat. If it were lit

chunks.en: If it was heated with olive pulp or wood,
chunks.st: with pomace or with wood,

chunks.en: it is like an oven.
chunks.st: its legal status is like that of an oven
chunks.stMore: and it is prohibited to place a pot atop it on Shabbat.

summary: We may not cook an egg by putting it near a hot urn, or by wrapping it in hot cloths or burying it in hot sand. Rabbi Yosei allows the hot cloths.
stIntro: In addition to the halakhot that deal with cooking on the fire on Shabbat, several related halakhot are discussed. The mishna says:

chunks.en: We may not put an egg next to
chunks.st: One may not place a raw egg next to

chunks.en: the hot-water urn so that it will roast.
chunks.st: an urn full of hot water so that it will roast slightly.

chunks.en: And one may not crack it into hot cloths.
chunks.st: And one may not even wrap it in cloths,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one may not heat the egg inside cloths that were heated in the sun.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yosei allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei permits doing so in that case. And, similarly,

chunks.en: And one may not bury it in sand or in road dust
chunks.st: one may not insulate it in sand or in road dust that was heated in the sun

chunks.en: so that it will roast.
chunks.st: so that it will roast.
chunks.stMore: Although there is no actual cooking with fire here, it is similar to cooking and the Sages issued a decree to prohibit doing so.

summary: The people of Teveryah ran a pipe of cold water through the hot springs to warm it on Shabbos. The Sages said that the water is forbidden. The mishnah also talks about two kinds of water-heating pots.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא וְהֵבִיאוּ סִלּוֹן
chunks.en: Once the people of Teveryah brought a pipe
chunks.st: a story about the people of the city of Tiberias, and they ran a cold-water pipe [silon]

chunks.he: שֶׁל צוֹנֵן לְתוֹךְ אַמָּה שֶׁל חַמִּין.
chunks.en: of cold water through a channel of hot water.
chunks.st: through a canal of hot
chunks.stMore: water from the Tiberias hot springs. They thought that by doing so, they could heat the cold potable water on Shabbat.

chunks.en: The Sages said to them:
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to them:

chunks.en: If it was on Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the water passed through on Shabbat, its legal status is

chunks.en: it is like water that was heated on Shabbos,
chunks.st: like that of hot water that was heated on Shabbat, and the water is

chunks.en: and it is forbidden for washing and for drinking.
chunks.st: prohibited both for bathing and for drinking. And if the water passed through

chunks.en: If it was on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: on a Festival,

chunks.en: it is like water that was heated on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: then it is prohibited for bathing

chunks.en: it is forbidden for washing but allowed for drinking.
chunks.st: but permitted for drinking.
chunks.stMore: On Festivals, one is even permitted to boil water on actual fire for the purposes of eating and drinking. In this mishna, the Sages discuss two vessels used for heating water.

chunks.en: A mulyar whose coals were swept out,
chunks.st: With regard to a mulyar, a bronze vessel into which coals are placed in an outer compartment and water is placed into an adjacent inner compartment, whose coals were swept,

words.note: A metal water pot with a place for coals.

chunks.en: we may drink from it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: one may drink from it on Shabbat.

chunks.en: An antichi, even though its coals were swept out,
chunks.st: With regard to an antikhi, which is a vessel with a different configuration, even if its coals were swept,

words.note: A different kind of water heater that keeps its heat longer.

chunks.en: we may not drink from it.
chunks.st: one may not drink from it on Shabbat.

summary: Cold water may not be put into a hot urn to heat it, and spices may not be put into a boiling pot, because that is cooking. But we may warm water a little, and put spices into a bowl.
stIntro: The Sages added to the laws of leaving food on a source of heat and cooking food on Shabbat:

chunks.en: An urn that was emptied,
chunks.st: An urn that was emptied of its hot water on Shabbat,

chunks.he: לֹא יִתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ צוֹנֵן בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ,
chunks.en: one may not put cold water into it so that it will get hot,
chunks.st: one may not place cold water into it so that the cold water will be heated.

chunks.en: but one may put it into it
chunks.st: However, one may place cold water into an urn or

chunks.en: or into a cup to make it lukewarm.
chunks.st: into a cup that were emptied of their hot water in order to warm it
chunks.stMore: but not in order to heat it. In continuation of the discussion of vessels where the prohibition of cooking applies even though the vessels are not actually on the fire itself, the mishna establishes:

chunks.en: A pan or a pot that he took off the fire while boiling,
chunks.st: A stew pot [ilpas] and a pot that were removed from the fire while they were still boiling, even if they were removed before Shabbat,

chunks.en: one may not put spices into them,
chunks.st: one may not place spices into them
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat itself. Even though the pot is not actually standing on the fire, the spices are still cooked in it because the pot is a primary vessel, i.e., a vessel whose contents were cooked on the fire.

chunks.en: but he may put them into
chunks.st: However, one may place the spices

chunks.en: a bowl or a serving dish.
chunks.st: into a bowl or into a tureen [tamḥui],
chunks.stMore: which is a large bowl into which people pour the contents a stew pot or a pot. Bowls and tureens are both secondary vessels and food placed into them does not get cooked.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he may put them into anything,
chunks.st: One may place spices into anything on Shabbat

chunks.he: חוּץ מִדָּבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ חֹמֶץ וְצִיר:
chunks.en: except something that has vinegar or fish brine in it.
chunks.st: except for a vessel that has in it something containing vinegar or brine of salted fish.

summary: This mishnah teaches about a vessel to catch dripping oil or sparks from a lamp, and which lamps may be moved on Shabbos. We may not put water in it, because that would put out the sparks.
stIntro: From a discussion of the halakhot of insulation and preparation for Shabbat followed by a brief tangent dealing with the prohibited labor of cooking on Shabbat, the mishna proceeds to briefly discuss prohibitions relating to set-aside [muktze] items in terms of Shabbat lamps.

chunks.en: We may not put a vessel under the lamp
chunks.st: One may not place a vessel beneath the oil lamp,
chunks.stMore: the vessel containing the oil and the wick, on Shabbat in order

chunks.en: to catch the oil in it.
chunks.st: to receive the oil that drips from the wick.

chunks.en: And if he put it there while it was still day,
chunks.st: And if one placed the vessel on Friday while it was still day,

chunks.en: it is allowed. But we may not use the oil,
chunks.st: it is permitted. However, in any case, one may not make use of the oil on Shabbat

chunks.en: because it was not prepared for Shabbos.
chunks.explain: The oil was set aside only for lighting.
chunks.st: because it is not from the oil prepared
chunks.stMore: from Shabbat eve for use on Shabbat. The oil in the lamp was already set aside and designated solely for the purpose of lighting the lamp. The dispute in this mishna seems to be a local one; however, it is the key to several halakhot in the area of the prohibition of set-aside [muktze].

chunks.en: We may move a new lamp,
chunks.st: One may move a new oil lamp on Shabbat

chunks.en: but not an old one.
chunks.explain: An old lamp is dirty with soot.
chunks.st: but not an old
chunks.stMore: one that was already used. A lamp that was used is covered with soot and unsuitable for use. It is therefore considered set aside from use due to its disgusting nature.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: we may move all lamps,
chunks.st: All oil lamps may be moved on Shabbat

chunks.en: except a lamp that is burning on Shabbos.
chunks.st: except for an oil lamp that is burning on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: due to the concern that it might be extinguished.

chunks.he: נוֹתְנִין כְּלִי תַחַת הַנֵּר לְקַבֵּל נִיצוֹצוֹת.
chunks.en: We may put a vessel under the lamp to catch sparks.
chunks.st: One may place a vessel beneath the oil lamp in order to receive burning sparks
chunks.stMore: of oil that fall from the lamp so that they will not cause a fire.

chunks.en: But one may not put water into it,
chunks.st: And he may not place water into the vessel

chunks.en: because that puts out the sparks.
chunks.st: because he thereby extinguishes the sparks.
